context:
Wheel exclusion via [tool.setuptools.packages.find] exclude (NOT MANIFEST.in)
+ optional-extra marker + conditional imports. No new packages, no
extraction, no compatibility shims. If wheel exclusion UX is unsatisfactory
(confirmed in w1a), fall back to conditional imports only (w2, w3).
description:
The `benchbox.monitoring` package (~2,000 lines) ships in the installable
wheel and is auto-enabled by the runner. It has only one external dependency
(`benchbox.utils.clock.mono_time`) and integrates with 3 core files
(runner.py, dataframe_runner.py, progress.py).

The coupling is light, but monitoring ships to all users even though it is
not required for core benchmarking. The proportionate fix is to:

1. Exclude `benchbox.monitoring` from the default wheel by adding it to the
   `exclude` list in `[tool.setuptools.packages.find]` in pyproject.toml.
   NOTE: MANIFEST.in controls sdist content only, not wheel content.
2. Add a `monitoring = []` optional extra in pyproject.toml as an intent
   marker. This signals the feature exists and reserves the extra name for
   a future separate distribution. It cannot re-include excluded wheel
   content - users who want monitoring from a wheel install would need a
   separate package or a source checkout.
3. Make the runner's monitoring imports conditional (graceful degradation
   when monitoring is not importable).

Simpler alternative: skip step 1 (keep monitoring in the wheel) and only
do step 3. This achieves graceful degradation without any packaging
complexity. Choose this path if the packaging investigation (w1a) reveals
the wheel-exclusion UX is not worth the tradeoff.

A full standalone `runwatch` package is not justified for ~2,000 lines with
one consumer.

work_units.notes:
Decision: skip wheel exclusion (w2). benchbox.monitoring has no external
dependencies, so wheel exclusion provides no install-size or dependency
benefit worth the confusing `monitoring = []` extra that installs nothing
(pip extras add dependencies, not source files). Proceeding with
conditional imports only (w3, w4) - this achieves graceful degradation
without packaging complexity.
work_units.summary: Research correct wheel-exclusion mechanism and decide on scope

work_units.notes:
In pyproject.toml [tool.setuptools.packages.find]:
  Add `"benchbox.monitoring"` and `"benchbox.monitoring.*"` to the
  `exclude` list (alongside existing `benchbox.release` entries).
In pyproject.toml [project.optional-dependencies]:
  Add `monitoring = []` as an intent marker. This is a placeholder - it
  cannot re-include excluded wheel content without a separate distribution.
  It reserves the extra name and signals the feature exists.
Do NOT edit MANIFEST.in - it has no effect on wheel content.
Verify exclusion: `uv build --wheel && unzip -l dist/*.whl | grep -c monitoring`
should return 0.
Skip this unit entirely if w1 decides wheel exclusion is not worth it.
work_units.summary: Apply packaging changes: exclude monitoring from wheel, add optional extra marker
